title: On Permitting no visits after dark
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：permit　|　正文 332 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 permit 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the nurse ① permitted no visits after dark at once, and every sufferer in the ward said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three nights on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the nurse ② permits no visits after dark in the rain without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ permit no visits after dark at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ permitted no visits after dark before — a line in the report for April 1949 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Permitting no visits after dark at once, the nurse said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the thermometer at the far cupboard, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ permit of another way entirely in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Permit of another way entirely at once and never mention it again.

By 1962 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the report, and a new sufferer from the next ward ⑧ permits of another way entirely at once every night without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the cupboard, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ permitted no visits after dark again when nobody else would.

⑩ To permit no visits after dark, my mother said in 1967, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the ward remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the ward forgets, somebody permits no visits after dark in the rain again and somebody must permit no visits after dark at once all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 允许（一般过去式 permitted no visits after dark：1955 年护士头一回这样做，二话不说地）
B. v. 允许（一般现在 permits no visits after dark：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 允许（不定式 to permit no visits after dark：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 允许（过去完成时 had permitted no visits after dark：1949 年四月的护理记录上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 允许（动名词 permitting no visits after dark 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 容许（permit of another way entirely：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去容许容许完全不同的一套做法）
G. v. 容许（permit of another way entirely：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 允许（后段两处：新来的病患照例 permits of another way entirely，而母亲又一次 permitted no visits after dark）

answers.why: permit 意为“允许”，1955 年护士二话不说地允许天黑以后不许人来访，那是病房里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 permitted。
permit 意为“允许”，自那以后护士淋着雨把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 permits。
permit 意为“允许”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯允许天黑以后不许人来访”，此处为不定式 to permit no visits after dark。
permit 意为“允许”，护理记录里 四月 那行字说明早在 1962 年之前就有人允许过，故用过去完成时 had permitted。
permit 意为“允许”，护士说“允许天黑以后不许人来访这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 permitting no visits after dark 作主语。
permit 意为“容许”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去容许容许完全不同的一套做法”，should ever 之后用原形 permit of another way entirely。
permit 意为“容许”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻容许容许完全不同的一套做法（permit of another way entirely at once），以后再也不要提起。
permit 意为“允许”，新来的病患每个夜晚都照例容许容许完全不同的一套做法，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 permits。
permit 意为“允许”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次二话不说地允许天黑以后不许人来访，用一般过去式 permitted 叙述。
permit 意为“允许”，结尾那句是母亲 1967 年的话：要允许天黑以后不许人来访，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和病房记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 permit 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1955 the nurse permitted no visits after dark at once, and nobody in the ward forgot it.
Even now the nurse permits no visits after dark in the rain whenever the ward asks.
Permitting no visits after dark at once, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever permit of another way entirely in the rain, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new sufferer from the next ward permits of another way entirely at once every night, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother permitted no visits after dark again, and the ward remembered that half.
